records.shared_stimulus: A cart changes velocity from 2 m/s east to 10 m/s east in 4 s, then later turns while keeping the same speed.
parts: (a) Identify the initial velocity, final velocity, and time for the first interval.
(b) Calculate the acceleration for the first interval.
(c) Carry your result from (b) forward to describe what the positive sign means in the chosen east-positive frame.
(d) Explain why the later turn is also acceleration even if speed stays constant.
records.student_text:
A cart changes velocity from 2 m/s east to 10 m/s east in 4 s, then later turns while keeping the same speed.
(a) Identify the initial velocity, final velocity, and time for the first interval.
(b) Calculate the acceleration for the first interval.
(c) Carry your result from (b) forward to describe what the positive sign means in the chosen east-positive frame.

records.student_html:
A cart changes velocity from 2 m/s east to 10 m/s east in 4 s, then later turns while keeping the same speed.

  1. Identify the initial velocity, final velocity, and time for the first interval.
  2. Calculate the acceleration for the first interval.
  3. Carry your result from (b) forward to describe what the positive sign means in the chosen east-positive frame.
  4. Explain why the later turn is also acceleration even if speed stays constant.
Show your reasoning here.
records.answer: 2 m/s, 10 m/s, 4 s; +2 m/s²; velocity becomes more positive/eastward; a direction change changes velocity.

records.primary_i_can: I can explain that acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.
records.evidence_job: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_action: Use the scenario evidence to make a physics claim and explain why it is consistent with the target.
records.intended_reasoning: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_text: A skateboarder moves east while slowing down. State the direction of the skateboarder’s velocity and acceleration, and explain why the skateboarder is accelerating even though speed decreases.
records.student_html: A skateboarder moves east while slowing down. State the direction of the skateboarder’s velocity and acceleration, and explain why the skateboarder is accelerating even though speed decreases.
records.answer: Velocity is east; acceleration is west. Acceleration is any change in velocity, including a decrease in speed.
records.solution_text: To slow an object moving east, acceleration must point opposite the velocity. A change in velocity magnitude is acceleration.
records.solution_html: To slow an object moving east, acceleration must point opposite the velocity. A change in velocity magnitude is acceleration.
